title: Updating an Existing Utility Cadastre Using Mobile LiDAR and GPR: Workflow and Cost Analysis for a Peri-Urban Gas Distribution Area

record.title: Updating an Existing Utility Cadastre Using Mobile LiDAR and GPR: Workflow and Cost Analysis for a Peri-Urban Gas Distribution Area
record.abstract: Periodic cadastre updates are required when network extensions or repairs alter buried asset positions. This paper presents a workflow that couples a vehicle-mounted LiDAR scanner for above-ground reference frame acquisition with GPR for subsurface detection, tested on 18 km of peri-urban gas distribution network in Sremska Mitrovica, Serbia. LiDAR point clouds were georeferenced using GNSS/INS at 5 cm absolute accuracy and served as the spatial backbone onto which GPR detections were registered. Change detection between the updated cadastre and the prior 2011 record identified 64 newly installed segments, 11 relocated segments and 3 abandoned segments not recorded in any documentation. Cost comparison against a conventional resurvey using walking GPR and RTK-GNSS on the same corridor showed a 34% reduction in field time per kilometre, partially offset by higher data processing costs. The workflow is applicable to annual update cycles for medium-density distribution grids.
